title: Ephemeral Mirroring + Probation Routing for Dedicated Evacuations
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: During planned or unplanned evacuations of dedicated capacity (maintenance, preemption, thermal events) we currently flip traffic to hosted in a blunt way that can either overload hosted or cause quality/latency regressions for tenants. Goal: introduce a low-risk, observable mechanism that (1) mirrors a small fraction of tenant traffic to hosted to warm caches and validate model-variant compatibility, and (2) places tenants into a short probation routing window where a controlled fraction of live requests are served by hosted variants with variant-ranking constraints until a graceful handoff is safe. This ticket implements the runtime + control-plane pieces for ephemeral mirroring and probation routing, plus telemetry, rollout controls, and rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Able to mirror sampled requests (configurable rate) from dedicated nodes to hosted replicas without increasing tail latency for the original request path
Probation routing state machine can place tenant routes into 'probation' for N minutes with configurable sample rates and variant filters
Variant-ranking rules can restrict which hosted model variants are eligible during probation (e.g., same architecture, max-quantization-level)
KV/cache warm-up effect observed in hosted replicas for mirrored traffic (telemetry shows KV cache hit increase > 10% over baseline after 15 min of mirroring)
Telemetry dashboard surfaces latency delta, token overhead, quality drift (against eval prompt set), and cost delta per tenant
Automated rollback triggers implemented: error-rate increase > 3% OR 2x median-latency over SLO OR quality regression > 5% on eval set
Security review completed for handshake tokens and mirrored payload handling (no sensitive data leaked; mirrors respect tenant data-egress flags)
Admin Console controls to start/stop probation per-tenant and adjust mirror rate are present and respect RBAC
updates: 2026-02-15 - Asha Patel: Initial design spike completed. Two approaches evaluated: in-path synchronous mirroring (adds latency risk) vs async fire-and-forget mirroring with eventual consistency for KV warming. Recommendation: async mirroring to avoid tail-latency exposure.

2026-02-20 - Liam O'Neill: Prototype implemented in the router: sampling hook emits mirror events to hosted ingress with a handshake token. Token TTL and signed nonce added to avoid replay. Prototype configured at 5% default mirror rate.

2026-02-25 - Security review requested by Liam O'Neill. Noted requirement: mirrored payloads must filter PII and observe tenant egress flags. Security flagged that handshake token lifecycle must be auditable.

2026-03-02 - Design review with PM (Rosa Nguyen) and Observability (Diego Ramos). Agreed on variant-ranking semantics: hosted variants must match model family and have quantization level >= tenant-minimum. Also agreed to add a "probation score" metric composed of latency delta, error delta, and quality delta.

2026-03-05 - Perf tests in staging: Mirroring at 5% produced measurable KV warm-up on hosted replicas without affecting median latency on dedicated. Cost overhead tracked; extrapolated to 0.8% increase for a 10% mirror rate across tenants. Initial canary enabled for tenant org-159.
2026-03-08 - Code review feedback (PR infra#2402): change mirror queue to backpressure under host ingress saturation, add hysteresis to probation exit rules. PR updated.

2026-03-10 - Liam O'Neill: Security review completed; mitigation implemented to strip sensitive metadata and log redaction applied. Preparing UI controls for Console team. Next: broader canary across three low-traffic regions and run synthetic quality checks.

Follow-ups: Console feature ticket for per-tenant probation controls; budget tracking ticket to classify mirror cost to tenant vs platform; add long-term policy for automatic probation after repeated evacuations.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (router) - implement sampling hook and async mirror emitter, signed handshake token generation, mirror queue with circuit-breaker
Phase 2 (runtime) - variant-ranking filter in hosted ingress, eviction/hysteresis logic to avoid flapping, KV-cache warm-up telemetry hooks
Phase 3 (control-plane) - probation state machine per-tenant, Console APIs to start/stop probation and set mirror rates
Phase 4 (observability) - dashboards: probation-score, mirrored-token-count, delta-latency, quality-regression; alerting rules and rollback automations
Phase 5 (canary & rollout) - 1 tenant -> 5 tenants -> regional ramp with rollback checks and post-rollout retrospective
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Chose async mirroring to prevent adding tail latency to the original request; tradeoff is eventual KV consistency rather than immediate cache parity
Default mirror rate 5% balances warm-up signal vs cost; configurable per-tenant because some tenants opt-in for faster warmups
Probation windows are timeboxed (default 10 minutes) with hysteresis to avoid repeated short cycles; longer windows increase cost but stabilize behavior
Variant-ranking restricts to compatible hosted variants to limit quality regressions, at the cost of reducing fallback capacity in some regions
We will attribute mirror costs to the platform by default but expose a tag so customers can opt to pay for faster handoffs
test_plan: Unit tests for sampling, handshake token generation/validation, and mirror-queue backpressure
Integration tests between router -> hosted ingress verifying variant-ranking enforcement and KV-warmup metrics
Staging perf runs with synthetic traffic at multiple mirror rates to validate median/tail latency and cost delta
Quality regression harness using tenant-specific eval set to detect content/score drift during probation
Chaos test: simulated dedicated-node evacuation while probation is enabled to validate graceful handoff and automatic rollback
playbook: How to start probation for a tenant: Console -> Tenant -> Routing -> Enable probation (sets mirror rate and window)
Operator rollback: If probation-score breaches threshold, Console shows auto-suggested rollback -> click to disable probation and purge mirrored KV entries on hosted nodes
Incident runbook: If hosted ingress is saturated by mirrors, reduce global mirror rate to 1%, disable non-critical tenant probation, and open capacity-scaling playbook
